p.scope-of-this-document: **Scope of this document.** This file defines what happens to a comparative research document *after* it is written: how a numbered delta becomes a decision, what becomes of the deltas that are declined, when a study goes stale and how it is refreshed, and the single honesty rule that keeps the whole genre from decaying into advocacy.

pipeline.title: The pipeline

p.A-RESEARCH-DOCUMENT-ENDS-IN-A-DELTA-TABL: A research document ends in a table of numbered deltas.

pipeline.fence: delta (proposed in the study) │ ▼ owner review ──► accepted ──► recorded decision + revisit trigger │ (leaves the study; lands in the spec) ▼ rejected ──► stays in the study, with its rejection reason (the study is the archive of roads not taken)

p.NOTHING-ON-THE-ACCEPTED-BRANCH-HAPPENS-I: Nothing on the accepted branch happens inside the research document — that is the deltas-not-decrees law ([protocol §law-deltas](COMPARATIVE-RESEARCH-PROTOCOL.xml#law-deltas)).

p.DELTAS-DO-NOT-RATIFY-OR-AUTO-SCHEDULE-TH: The deltas do not ratify themselves and they do not auto-schedule.

p.a-human-decides-one-of-lead: A human reads the numbered table and, per delta, decides one of:

td.fact: Stays in the study with a reason (below)
Stays as a delta, marked *deferred*, with a revisit trigger

p.A-DELTA-WITH-NO-VERDICT-IS-NOT-DONE-BEIN: A delta with no verdict is not done being reviewed.

p.the-value-of-the-numbering: The value of the numbering is exactly this: the owner can say "accept D1, reject D4, defer D7" and every party knows precisely which proposal is meant.

p.AN-ACCEPTED-DELTA-LANDS-AS-A-RECORDED-DE: An accepted delta does not just get "implemented" — it lands as a **recorded decision with a revisit trigger**, at the spec anchor the delta named as its target home.

p.this-is-decision-records-doing-its-job: This is `flow:decision-records` doing its job: the delta's argument (why match the competitor here) becomes the record's *Why*, and the delta's number and the study's title become the citation.

p.a-recorded-decision-carries-lead: A recorded decision born from an accepted delta carries:

facts.RECORD-FIELD-DECISION: **Decision** — the capability we will build, one line.
facts.RECORD-FIELD-WHY: **Why** — the gap the study found, cited back to the quoted evidence in the research doc (the verbatim quote is the data).
facts.RECORD-FIELD-CONSIDERED-AND-REJECTED: **Considered and rejected** — including "do nothing", if the study weighed it.
facts.RECORD-FIELD-WHEN-TO-REVISIT: **When to revisit** — a trigger, because a competitive gap can close from either side: they might drop the feature, or the space might move.

p.THE-STUDY-NOTES-THE-ACCEPTANCE-AND-POINT: The research document then notes, at the delta, that it was accepted and points at the decision's anchor.

p.THE-DELTA-IS-HISTORY-IN-THE-STUDY-AND-LI: The delta is now *history* in the study and *live* in the spec.

rejected.title: Rejected deltas stay in the study

p.it-stays-annotated-with-the-reason-lead: It stays in the research document, annotated with the reason it lost:

rejected.fence: ### D4 — Background auto-update daemon Maps to §3.4. **Priority:** LOW. **Verdict: REJECTED (2026-07-05).** For a tool whose value is an audit trail, silent background updates are the wrong default; every install should be deliberated. Revisit only if users ask for it.

p.THE-DOCUMENT-IS-ALSO-THE-ARCHIVE-OF-ROAD: The research document is **also the archive of roads not taken**.

p.a-rejected-delta-answers-the-question-be: A rejected delta left in place answers the question before it is re-asked: the next person who says "why don't we just add auto-update like they have" reads D4 and gets the reason in one read instead of re-running the analysis.

p.deleting-the-delta-deletes-the-immunity: Delete the rejected delta and you delete the immunity; the question comes back every quarter.

p.THE-REJECTION-REASON-MUST-CITE-SOMETHING: The rejection reason is subject to the same standard as a decision's *Why*: cite something.

p.a-cited-rejection-closes-the-question: "Rejected because it's bad" invites the delta to be re-proposed; "rejected because it contradicts the audit-trail invariant" closes it.

p.A-STUDY-IS-A-DATED-SNAPSHOT: A comparative study is a **dated snapshot**, and the subject keeps shipping.

quote.A-STUDY-OLDER-THAN-THE-LAST-MAJOR-RELEAS: A study **older than its subject's last major release** is stale-flagged.

facts.STALE-REFRESH-VIA-THE-RE-FETCH-LIST: **Refresh via the re-fetch list**, not by rewriting. Walk the URLs in the study's re-fetch section, re-capture the quotes, record the new access dates and the new subject version.
facts.STALE-APPEND-DONT-OVERWRITE: **Append, don't overwrite.** Add a dated refresh block noting what changed materially since the last capture. Keep the old capture as a historical baseline — the point of an evergreen doc is that the old snapshot still has value.
facts.STALE-RE-AUDIT-THE-DELTA-TABLE: **Re-audit the delta table.** Every delta gets re-checked against the new reality:
facts.RE-AUDIT-A-GAP-THE-SUBJECT-WIDENED: A trailing gap the subject *widened* → the delta's priority may rise.
facts.RE-AUDIT-A-GAP-THE-SUBJECT-CLOSED: A gap the subject *closed on their side* (dropped the feature) → the delta may become moot; mark it so.
facts.RE-AUDIT-A-GAP-WE-CLOSED: A gap *we* closed (shipped the capability) → the delta is done; point it at the shipped decision.
facts.RE-AUDIT-A-WHOLLY-NEW-CAPABILITY: A wholly new capability → a new delta.

p.refreshing-is-cheaper-because-laws-one-a: Refreshing is cheaper than re-studying precisely because Law 1 and Law 5 did their work:

facts.REFRESH-CHEAP-THE-VERSION-NUMBER-IS-ON-R: and the previous version number is on record.

p.A-STUDY-WITHOUT-A-RE-FETCH-LIST-CANNOT-B: A study written without a re-fetch list cannot be refreshed — only redone.

p.one-rule-governs-the-whole-genre-lead: One rule governs the whole genre, and it is worth stating alone:

quote.THE-HONESTY-RULE: A study that only finds gaps where we trail is marketing for the competitor. A study that only finds where we lead is marketing for us. Neither is intelligence.

p.THE-TWO-WAY-LAW-IS-NOT-A-FORMATTING-CONV: The two-way law ([protocol §law-two-way](COMPARATIVE-RESEARCH-PROTOCOL.xml#law-two-way)) is not a formatting convention — it is the difference between a document you can act on and a document that flatters a foregone conclusion.

p.trail-only-studies-talk-teams-into-copyi: Trail-only studies talk teams into copying features they do not need.

p.lead-only-studies-talk-teams-out-of-a-re: Lead-only studies talk teams out of taking a real threat seriously.

p.both-feel-like-analysis-while-producing-: Both feel like analysis while producing the opposite.

p.THE-TEST-AT-REVIEW-TIME: The test at review time: **read §3 and §4 side by side.**

p.a-lopsided-study-is-advocacy: If one is three pages and the other is three lines, the study is advocacy wearing the genre's clothes.

p.no-two-teams-make-all-the-same-decisions: A real study of a real competitor finds meaningful gaps in both directions, because no two teams make all the same decisions — where they diverged is exactly what the study exists to surface.

facts.SUM-THE-STUDY-PROPOSES-THE-OWNER-REVIEWS: The study proposes numbered deltas; the owner reviews each and accepts, rejects, or defers it.
facts.SUM-AN-ACCEPTED-DELTA-BECOMES-A-DECISION: An accepted delta becomes a recorded decision with a revisit trigger at its target anchor — `flow:decision-records` does the landing; the study points at the anchor.
facts.SUM-A-REJECTED-DELTA-STAYS-WITH-ITS-REAS: A rejected delta stays in the study with its cited reason; the document is the archive of roads not taken.
facts.SUM-A-STALE-STUDY-IS-REFRESHED-AND-RE-AU: A study older than its subject's last major release is stale-flagged, refreshed via the re-fetch list (append, don't overwrite), and its delta table re-audited.
facts.SUM-THE-HONESTY-RULE: The honesty rule: trail-only is marketing for them, lead-only is marketing for us. Read §3 and §4 side by side — if they are not both substantial, send the study back.
